facts.fact: Thabethe and Mathews (University of the Western Cape) state that all public health facilities in Eastern Cape province use DHIS2 to collect and report routine health data; the province has 860 public facilities (727 primary health care clinics, 41 community health centres, 92 hospitals), of which 850 are registered in the national data dictionary and expected to report monthly. One province only; study period April 2017 to March 2020.

The authors state that clinicians record into patient records and tick registers, the data is consolidated monthly onto a facility input form, and it is then captured into DHIS2 by a dedicated, DHIS2-trained information cadre appointed or seconded in the health facility, citing the national department's 2012 and 2013 standard operating procedures. Eastern Cape, April 2017 to March 2020.

The authors state that all public health facilities in Eastern Cape use DHIS2, with capture by staff in the facility; in their sample of 265 of 850 facilities, 9,489 of 9,540 expected monthly reports were received (99.5%) over April 2017 to March 2020, while data-element completeness was 49.7% and overall data completeness 74.6%. The share is of all public facilities in one province, not of primary clinics nationally, and mobile clinics, satellite clinics and health posts were excluded from the sample.

The authors state that the National Department of Health decided in 2017 to upgrade from the standalone DHIS to DHIS2 and adopted it as the priority information system, and that the Eastern Cape Department of Health officially adopted online DHIS2 in 2017 on the national department's instruction.
